title: vector_add kernel produces wrong result / HIP illegal address for aligned N
description: The vector_add<<<>>> kernel launched for N=262144 sporadically returns a wrong first element and, under some warm-up conditions, triggers hipErrorIllegalAddress on hipDeviceSynchronize(). Correctness check reports FAIL_NUMERIC with max_abs_err in the low e-3 range even though the input arrays only reach ~524 in magnitude. Behavior is deterministic across runs when the OOB write happens to hit an unmapped page.
expected_behavior: STATUS: PASS with max_abs_err < 1e-4 for every element c[i] = a[i] + b[i].
actual_behavior: Either STATUS: FAIL_NUMERIC (garbage at boundary elements) or STATUS: FAIL_RUNTIME with HIP_ERR: hipErrorIllegalAddress.
reproduction_hints: Look at the grid-stride loop bound — `for (int i = tid; i <= N; ...)` includes index N.
Buffer allocation is only N * sizeof(float), so index N is one element past the end.
Fix candidate: change `<= N` to `< N`.
